amendments.normalized_body: CleanFilter action in engine.rs:346-368 silently destroys nitrogen and carbon: microbe biomass is reduced by `intensity * 0.5` but the removed mass is not routed to any pool (fine_detritus, DON/DOC, etc.). This is an N/C conservation violation. The removed biomass should be routed to `fine_detritus_g_total` via `live_biomass_detrital_mass_g()` (same pattern used for shrimp mortality at shrimp.rs:483-491), or alternatively tracked as an explicit budget export if the intent is that filter-rinsing removes matter from the system entirely.

Conservation tests (test_closed_system_c_conservation, test_closed_system_n_conservation) only exercise the code-default ProcessParams which sets `respiration_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour = 0.0` and `photosynthesis_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour = 0.0` (process.rs:187-188). The actual data preset (default.toml:9-10) sets these to 0.08 and 0.12 respectively. When loaded from presets, the chemistry system (chemistry.rs:31-47) adds/removes DIC without a compensating organic-C change, breaking carbon conservation by milligrams per tick. Add a comment or separate test acknowledging that the hourly DIC respiration/photosynthesis flux is an intentional atmospheric-exchange simplification and that closed-system carbon conservation holds only when these rates are zero.

SiphonDetritus action in engine.rs:342-346 silently destroys nitrogen and carbon: `particulate_organics_g_total` and `fine_detritus_g_total` are reduced by `fraction` without routing the removed mass anywhere. Like CleanFilter, this is a physical export that should either be routed explicitly or return a BudgetDelta with the export amount so the ledger records a classified outflow rather than an unexplained mass loss.

Fix closed-system mass creation in `system:daily_shrimp`. In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:354` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:371`, a resolved clutch adds `25` juveniles per successful berried female without debiting any explicit nitrogen/carbon source, so the new ledger violates the acceptance criterion once reproduction is enabled. Repro: starting from the existing shrimp fixture in `crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_population.rs:8`, a 60-day no-feed/no-water-change run with budget tracking ends with positive mass drift (`delta_n ~= 65.38 mg`, `delta_c ~= 408.62 mg`), and the first non-zero closed tick is `system:daily_shrimp` at about `+34.48 mg N / +215.52 mg C` per hatch. Model clutch/egg biomass as an explicit pool and include it in the canonical totals, or debit another explicit source on spawn/hatch, and add a regression in `crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:404` covering a reproducing shrimp tank with no feed/export.

Add an actual end-of-tick conservation guard when budget tracking is enabled. `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:164` and `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:168` only record and store the tick, while `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:141` uses only a `debug_assert!` for per-stage bookkeeping consistency. In release builds the ledger is passive, so non-conserving paths like the shrimp hatch case ship silently. Wire a tick-level closed-system check after invariants (or at least a test-only assert hooked into the tracked tick path) so a mass leak fails immediately instead of depending on ad hoc test coverage.
